title: slo: enforce request-level SLOs with circuit breakers and load-shedding + regional failover hotfix
author: Ava Martinez
description:
Motivation: During incident INT-2026-02-18 we observed cascading failures when overloaded edge routers exhausted downstream capacity. This PR adds request-level SLO enforcement surfaced to the router, a lightweight circuit breaker for unhealthy upstreams, token-bucket-based load-shedding for low-priority traffic, and a region-aware failover policy. The changes are gated behind feature flag 'slo_protect' (off by default) but the hotfix enables it by config during rollout. Summary of changes and rationale: 1) SLO enforcement (services/router/src/slo.rs) - track per-route request budgets based on configured SLOs; when budget is exhausted the router will short-circuit (reject with 429) or mark request for shedding based on route priority. This protects latency SLOs for high-priority traffic. 2) Circuit breaker (services/router/src/cb.rs) - add per-upstream CB with configurable failure thresholds, exponential backoff and manual override via admin API. Keeping CB state keyed by upstream id and instrumented with metrics. 3) Load-shedding (services/router/src/load_shed.rs) - implement token-bucket shedder with dynamic refill tuned by observed queueing; provides graceful degradation for best-effort traffic. 4) Regional failover (services/router + infra/k8s) - prefer local region but automatically failover to healthy regions when local SLOs are violated or circuit breakers trip. 5) Observability and alerts - add SLO violation metric, circuit_breaker.state tag, and an alert rule to catch when shed rate exceeds 5% for 5m. 6) Hotfix tuning - backoff/decay constants adjusted to avoid thundering rejoin. Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests for cb and load shedder
- [x] Deterministic integration test for regional failover
- [x] Metrics emitted for SLO violations and CB state
- [x] Updated alerts and runbook reference
- [x] Canary rollout validated in eu-west-1 then global rollout
Notes: This PR was developed under on-call constraints; changes are intentionally conservative and opt-in. Followup work (ENG-1209) will expose richer per-customer policies and self-serve thresholds.

Introduce token-bucket load shedder + unit tests
Wire SLO enforcement into request router and add config flags
Add region-aware failover policy and integration test

review_comments: Liam Chen (review): Overall looks good. One question about lock contention in cb.rs — can we avoid parking_lot in the hot path?
Ava Martinez (reply): Switched to atomics in commit 4 and added comment explaining memory ordering choice.
Samir Patel (review): Load shedder uses token bucket with dynamic target. Need a unit test that simulates burst and steady load to validate no starvation.
Ava Martinez (reply): Added deterministic unit test (tests/load_shed/unit_tests.rs) and refactored to make refill deterministic in test mode.
Rosa Diaz (approve): Approve after CI passes. Observability changes look reasonable and alerts tuned.
SRE (comment): Please ensure admin override endpoint has RBAC; flagged for followup but not blocking hotfix.
release_notes:
- Enforce request-level SLOs by rejecting or shedding low-priority requests when global SLOs are at risk.
- Add a circuit breaker implementation for per-route upstream failures with exponential backoff and manual override.
- Add region-aware failover policy that prefers local region but falls back to healthy regions under degraded conditions.
- Hotfix: backoff tuning to avoid thundering during failover.
- Metrics and alerts updated (new SLO violation metric and circuit_breaker.state tag).
files_summary: Minor API additions to router public interface; runtime behavior changes guarded by feature flag 'slo_protect' and default off for older deployments.
notes: This was a hotfix triggered by incident INT-2026-02-18; rollout completed via canary (eu-west-1) then full release. Consider backport to release/1.4 for Dedicated customers.
